content: Kong's built-in JWT plugin authenticates and forwards a fixed set of consumer headers upstream but does not natively remap arbitrary JWT claims to custom headers; that requires a small custom plugin (Lua or serverless-functions plugin) or a community plugin (kong-jwt2header, kong-plugin-jwt-claims-advanced) to copy specific claims into trusted X-* headers. Common pattern for this project: Kong verifies JWT, a thin Go BFF behind Kong re-parses the verified JWT (or Kong-forwarded consumer info) and sets X-User-Id/X-Operator-Id/X-Role headers, and downstream services trust those headers only when the request originates from the internal network/BFF, never from the public edge directly.
